findings.current: Namho, the old man in question, replied with a sour look.
findings.defect: Drops the narrator’s deliberately contradictory description of Namho as an old young man.
findings.rationale: 늙은 청년 preserves the joke that he is counted among the Pavilion’s young members despite his age.
findings.replacement: Namho, the old young man singled out, answered with a face like he’d bitten into something foul.
findings.source: 지목당한 늙은 청년, 남호가 똥 씹은 얼굴로 대꾸했다.

findings.current: I mean, why not say that from the start?
findings.defect: Reverses the complaint: Jin wishes Taishan had not spoken up at all.
findings.rationale: 처음부터 말이라도 하지 말든가 means he should have kept quiet from the outset, not said it sooner.
findings.replacement: I mean, if he was going to do that, why say anything in the first place?
findings.source: 아니, 이럴 거면 처음부터 말이라도 하지 말든가.

findings.current: I’ve told them more than once that they could go home, though I had no right to ask. But they’ve stayed with the family to the very end.
findings.defect: “I had no right to ask” makes his offer of departure sound like an improper request, obscuring his embarrassment at continuing to rely on them.
findings.rationale: 염치가 없어 expresses Tang Sadok’s sense that imposing on their generosity is shameless; he repeatedly gives them leave to return.
findings.replacement: I felt ashamed to keep relying on them, so I told them more than once that they were free to go… Yet they’ve stayed with our family all this time.
findings.source: 염치가 없어 몇 번이나 돌아가도 좋다고 했지만…… 그럼에도 끝까지 본가에 남아 있네.

findings.current: Back then, you were really…quite a character.
findings.defect: Softens Jin’s pointed reference to Tang Sadok’s difficult temper into a vague description.
findings.rationale: 한 성격 하다 refers to having a strong or difficult temper, which is the contrast driving Jin’s surprise at Tang Sadok’s change.
findings.replacement: Back then, you really…had quite a temper.
findings.source: 그때만 해도 진짜…… 한 성격 하셨었는데.

findings.current: “Is the…no, is my Master staying in the Rear Court?”
findings.defect: Omits Jin’s aborted familiar address before he corrects himself to “Master.”
findings.rationale: 노, 아니 스승님 preserves the audible self-correction and its shift in address.
findings.replacement: “Is the old—no, is my Master staying in the Rear Court?”

findings.current: And despite being over a hundred yards away, a voice boomed like thunder and reached my ears.
findings.defect: Changes the distance by treating 장 as a yard.
findings.rationale: A 장 is roughly 3.3 meters; 백여 장 is more than three hundred yards, not merely a hundred.
findings.replacement: And though I was more than three hundred yards away, a voice boomed like thunder and pierced my ears.
findings.source: 그리고 백여 장도 넘게 떨어져 있음에도, 천둥처럼 울려 퍼지는 목소리가 귓가를 파고든 것은.

findings.defect: “Ugly King” suggests physical appearance, while the coined title mocks Jeok Cheongang’s disgraceful display.
findings.rationale: The preceding 추하다 describes the embarrassing spectacle of the argument; the new epithet extends that judgment.

findings.current: I should’ve been moved that he’d come all this way for me, only to nag the Divine Physician like he was a peanut he could endlessly crack open.
findings.defect: Invents cracking open a peanut, replacing the image of relentlessly roasting or badgering someone.
findings.rationale: 땅콩처럼 달달 볶다 evokes persistent roasting and harrying, not cracking a peanut open.
findings.replacement: I should’ve been moved that he’d come all this way for me and was roasting the Divine Physician like a peanut over a fire. But it wasn’t easy.
findings.source: 나를 위해 여기까지 와서 신의를 땅콩처럼 달달 볶고 있는 모습에 감동해야 하는데 그게 참 쉽지가 않다.

summary: Several action and quantity errors, plus losses of characterization and comic meaning.
